human_tolerance.notes: Comes readily to winter feeders and forages in low vegetation; among the most susceptible North American birds to building collisions, which is high road and window mortality in an urban plot.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Breeds in central Canada and New England; Missouri birds are absent from late spring through early autumn.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Winters in the southern United States, foraging in flocks in low vegetation.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Autumn arrival and winter territories in the southern states.

vocalizations.description: At least two distinct songs: an initial note followed by three or so repeated notes a major third above, and a second with a note a whole step lower then a note a minor third below. Mnemonics are 'Po-or Sam Peabody, Peabody, Peabody' and 'O-oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada'; the rhythm is very regular and the timbre pinched, often sounding out of tune.
A short single-note call, one of at least two calls the species gives apart from its song; the behaviour program uses it when a predator comes close.

taxonomy.note: GBIF backbone and ITIS TSN 179462; the binomial was coined by Gmelin in 1789.

external.note: gbif_usage_key from the GBIF species/match API; wikidata and itis_tsn from the Wikidata item (P815) and confirmed against ITIS.

range.note: 'It breeds in northern North America and winters in the southern United States' - Canada and the United States.

traits.limb_count.note: A bird: two legs are the limbs.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'These birds forage on the ground under or near thickets or in low vegetation by kicking backward with both feet simultaneously', plus flight.

traits.nest_type.note: 'They nest either on the ground under shrubs or low in trees' - Ground recorded for the ground nest, which is the common case in a garden shrub.

traits.perching.note: Perches in thickets and low trees.

traits.size_class.note: Derived from mass_kg (0.026 kg is in the Tiny band).

traits.mass_kg.note: 'Typical weight is 22 to 32 g, with an average of 26 g.'

traits.lifespan_y.note: Judgement: the article records no wild lifespan for this species. Three years is an authored value for a small wintering sparrow; treat it as an estimate, not a sourced figure.

traits.diet.note: 'They mainly eat seeds, insects and berries'; insects make up a larger share in summer, so the seed share is weighted down in the summer months.

traits.social.note: Solitary or paired, aggregating in winter flocks; group_size 1-4 records the small winter groups rather than the whole flock.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Feeds by day in low vegetation.

traits.defense.note: Authored: flees into thickets when disturbed; no explicit escape behaviour is described in the article.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: approaches winter feeders closely but drops quickly when disturbed.

habitat.use.note: Ground and low-vegetation foraging under thickets, plus shrub perches; 70/30 is a judgement informed by EltonTraits.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Nests on the ground under shrubs and forages under or near thickets.

habitat.resources.note: Seed, insect and berry foods from the diet section, with the summer weighting from the same passage; nest and shelter tags from the breeding and foraging descriptions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Attracted to feeders and tolerant of suburban cover, with documented high collision mortality; numeric tolerances authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It breeds in northern North America and winters in the southern United States' - a migrant in Missouri.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding in central Canada and New England, winter flocks in the southern United States; the Missouri arrival and departure windows are a judgement from those two statements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Authored: egg, juvenile and adult; the article gives a clutch of three to five eggs but no incubation or fledging interval, so durations are left unset.

look.note: White-striped morph: black crown with a white central stripe, white supercilium, yellow lores, gray auriculars with a black eye line, a white throat, streaked gray-tan breast and rufous wings with two white wing bars; proportions authored (judgement).

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: seed foraging at the feeder, the distinctive song, and a nesting window matching the April-July breeding range. No alarm param is set, because the only call the article describes is the song.

vocalizations.alarm.note: 'The white-throated sparrow also has at least two calls, in addition to its song.' The page does not describe them; the alarm use, cooldown and loudness are authored judgement.
